role: individual original-hunk TypeScript definite-assignment source decision
subject: refactor(material/progress-spinner): fix strict property initialization errors
decision: The complete modern progress-spinner patch changes only definite-assignment annotations on two production fields and two upstream test fixture fields, with no initializer or executable statement. The owned historical spinner is separately implemented: its bound progress-spinner.ts retains the historical private _strokeWidth field and SVG implementation, and its HTML and SCSS are bound as owned source context. Preserve its existing contract without copying the modern component annotations. This source-only review does not establish runtime, current-peer inheritance, styles, the 21.x line, security clearance or G11. The current owned library compiler configuration explicitly disables strictPropertyInitialization; this does not assert that another compiler configuration will accept unmodified sources.

previous_disposition_record.reason: The diff in src/material/progress-spinner/progress-spinner.spec.ts changes `strokeWidth: number;`. The owned legacy file still contains the previous line because this package keeps the Material 16 legacy contract (zone scheduling, factory providers, explicit change detection, or the pre-signal API). The current-component rewrite is not copied into the legacy sources. The commit is an ancestor of v22.1.7, so @angular/material@22.1.7 and @angular/cdk@22.1.7 already contain it for peer callers.

limitations: No whole-application, rendered, runtime or installed-peer execution is claimed.
The owned Sass companion remains separately qualified; these TS annotation changes are not a Sass or theme test.
The actual upstream TypeScript compiler configuration is not transplanted.
